html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Why explicit criteria beat vague instructions and "be conservative"
  • How false positives destroy developer trust, and what to do about them
  • Severity criteria with concrete code examples
  • Few-shot examples: when, how many, and what they should show

2Explicit Criteria Beat Vague Instructions (Task 4.1)

Running case

Birchwood Supply's Review Bot Cries Wolf

  • The CI review bot comments on every pull request
  • Developers say "half the comments are noise" and have started ignoring all of them, including the real security findings
  • The prompt says: "Review the code and report issues. Be conservative; only report high-confidence findings."
Vague instruction Explicit criterion
"Check that comments are accurate" "Flag a comment only when the behavior it claims contradicts what the code actually does"
"Be conservative" / "only report high-confidence findings" "Report: bugs and security vulnerabilities. Skip: minor style and local naming patterns"
"Rate how severe it is" A severity table with a short code example for each level

  • General phrases such as "be conservative" or "only report high-confidence findings" do not improve precision: the model cannot calibrate "confidence" the way you imagine. Specific, categorical criteria do.
  • False positives are costly beyond the noise. A category with a high false-positive rate undermines trust in the accurate categories too.
  • If one category is noisy, temporarily disable it to restore trust while you improve its prompt, then re-enable it.
  • Severity levels need definitions and examples: for each level give a short concrete code example, so classification is consistent from run to run.
Report: SQL built by string concatenation (high); missing null check before dereference (medium).
Skip: variable naming, import order, formatting, patterns that match the file's existing style.
Severity high example:  query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=" + user_id
Severity low example:   a TODO comment without a ticket number
Exam tip

Asked how to reduce false positives? → specific criteria for what to report and skip, not "be more conservative" and not a confidence cutoff.

Exam tip

Severity that varies between runs needs a definition and a code example for each level.

3Few-Shot Prompting (Task 4.2)

Few-shot prompting puts a few worked examples of input and desired output in the prompt.

Use few-shot to... Detail
Get consistent format When detailed instructions still give inconsistent output, examples are the most effective technique
Show ambiguous cases Examples of tool selection for ambiguous requests, or branch-level test-coverage gaps
Generalize judgment Models apply the reasoning to novel patterns, not only to the examples listed
Reduce hallucination in extraction Show handling of informal measurements and varied document structures

  • How many: 2 to 4 targeted examples, aimed at the ambiguous situations (not easy cases).
  • Show the reasoning: state why one action was chosen over plausible alternatives.
  • Show the output format: location, issue, severity, suggested fix.
  • Contrast acceptable patterns with genuine issues so the model skips harmless code (fewer false positives) yet still generalizes.
  • Varied document structures (inline citations versus a bibliography; methodology sections versus details embedded in text) → examples with each structure.
  • Empty or null extraction of fields that exist in the source? Add examples from documents with varied formats showing the correct extraction.
Exam tip

Instructions alone give inconsistent output → few-shot examples. But a missing-information problem (the document does not contain the data) is not fixed by examples; see Modules 10 and 11.

4Exam Q&A

S1A review bot's developers ignore comments because many are false positives. The prompt says "only report high-confidence findings". What change is most effective?

  • AAsk it to attach a confidence number from 1 to 10 to each finding and filter out anything below 8
  • BTell the model to be even more conservative
  • CAdd explicit criteria that list which issue types to report (bugs, security) and which to skip (minor style, local patterns)
  • DLower the temperature to zero
Show the answer

Answer: C. Categorical criteria improve precision. General cautions and confidence filtering do not.

S2One category (naming comments) has a 60% false-positive rate, while the security category is accurate. Developers have started ignoring everything. What is the best short-term step?

  • ATemporarily disable the noisy category while improving its prompt
  • BTell developers to read every comment carefully, including the noisy ones
  • CRemove the security category too
  • DAdd more comments per file
Show the answer

Answer: A. Disabling a noisy category restores trust in the accurate ones while you fix it.

S3Severity labels vary between runs: the same missing check is "medium" once and "critical" the next time. What is the best fix?

  • ADefine each severity level with a concrete code example
  • BAsk for shorter output so that fewer severity labels need to be assigned
  • CRemove severity from the output
  • DUse all capitals in the prompt so the severity rules are taken seriously
Show the answer

Answer: A. Examples per level anchor the classification and make it consistent.

S4Detailed written instructions still produce inconsistent report formatting. What technique is the most effective next?

  • ARetrying until it looks right
  • BA longer system prompt with more adjectives and more emphatic wording
  • CFew-shot examples showing the exact desired output format
  • DA higher max_tokens limit so that the replies are never cut off
Show the answer

Answer: C. Examples demonstrate the format that prose fails to convey.

S5How many few-shot examples are typically best, and aimed at what?

  • AOne example of the easiest case
  • B2 to 4 targeted examples for ambiguous scenarios, with reasoning
  • C20 examples of simple cases
  • DNone, because examples make the model copy them and overfit to the sample
Show the answer

Answer: B. A few well-chosen examples of the ambiguous situations teach judgment.

S6An extraction prompt keeps returning empty values for "author" in documents where the author appears in different places. Which improvement fits?

  • AIncrease the document length
  • BMake the field required in the schema so that the model always has to fill it in for every document
  • CAdd few-shot examples of varied document formats showing the correct extraction
  • DRemove the author field
Show the answer

Answer: C. Examples from varied structures help the model find the field wherever it appears.

S7What is a benefit of including both acceptable code patterns and genuine issues in the examples?

  • AIt disables severity ratings
  • BIt makes responses longer
  • CThe model matches only those exact snippets and ignores any similar patterns
  • DIt reduces false positives while letting the model generalize to new patterns
Show the answer

Answer: D. Contrast examples teach the boundary between harmless and harmful code.

S8Which TWO changes most improve the precision of a review prompt? Select TWO.

  • AAsk for a confidence number and filter below a cutoff
  • BAsk it to review fewer files
  • CList the categories to report and the categories to skip
  • DTell the model to be conservative
  • EDefine each severity level with a code example
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. Categorical criteria and severity examples change what is reported. Vague caution and confidence filtering do not.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Explicit criteria Say what to report and what to skip; categorical beats "be conservative" or confidence cutoffs
Contradiction example Flag a comment only when its claim contradicts the code
False positives Hurt trust in all categories; temporarily disable a noisy one while you fix the prompt
Severity Define each level with a concrete code example
Few-shot Best for consistent format and ambiguous cases; 2 to 4 targeted examples with reasoning
Few-shot extras Show the target format; contrast acceptable vs genuine; varied document structures reduce empty extraction
